title: VPC upgrade canary with simulated network partitions and KMS rotation acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for performing Private/VPC control-plane and node upgrades using a small canary cohort that includes simulated network partition scenarios and an in-proc KMS key rotation. This ensures upgrades are safe for air-gapped and minimal-egress environments and that KMS rotations can be performed without customer-visible downtime or unexpected data loss.
background: Customers running Private/VPC deployments require near-zero disruption during upgrades and periodic KMS rotations. Recent incidents in staging exposed a class of failures where simulated intermittent network partitions caused canaries to diverge and then fail to recover cleanly. Separately, KMS rotations in isolated deployments required temporary outbound access or manual operator intervention. We need a reproducible, auditable acceptance suite and operational playbook to certify upgrades in constrained network environments.
proposal_summary: Ship a canary upgrade process that: (1) deploys upgrades to a configurable percentage of nodes (default 5%), (2) runs a pre-defined synthetic traffic and KV-cache warmup workload, (3) injects controlled network partitions and packet loss during the canary window, (4) performs an automated KMS rotation on the canary control plane and keys used by runtime components, and (5) runs verification and rollback automation based on SLOs and audit logs. The acceptance criteria below codify required behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout: upgrades must start with <=5% of cluster capacity and remain isolated from primary traffic until verification passes.
Synthetic workload: run a representative synthesis suite for at least 30 minutes that covers generation, chat, and embedding endpoints at production-like token length distributions.

Network partition simulation: during canary, inject controlled partitions (one-way and two-way) and 5-20% packet loss windows; canaries must resume normal operation and rejoin cluster state with no data loss after partitions are healed.
Latency and error SLOs: for the canary cohort p99 token latency must not exceed 2x baseline and end-to-end error rate must be <=0.5% for the duration of verification window.

KMS rotation: perform a key rotation against the canary's KMS keys with no customer-visible failures; all runtime components must re-encrypt/decrypt successfully and metrics/logs must show key rotation audit events.

Minimal egress path: any required egress for the rotation/upgrade must be restricted to a pre-approved proxy endpoint and documented; acceptance requires an explicit justification and temporary permit recorded in the audit trail.

Automatic rollback: if any critical threshold is exceeded (defined in test_plan) the system must automatically halt further rollout and trigger rollback to the previous pinned image within the rollback SLA.
Observability: upgrade must emit structured upgrade-step events, KMS events, and network-simulation markers; logs must include trace IDs enabling a single request replay through the upgrade timeline.
Artifact provenance: container images and artifacts used in the canary must be signed; image signatures must be validated before deployment in air-gapped mode.
Operator playbook: a documented, runbook-style playbook for manual intervention must exist and be validated in tabletop drills prior to GA release.
Auditability: after the canary completes, a report must be generated that includes metric deltas, event timelines, key rotation proof, and a signed operator approval or automated gate decision.
No manual secret injection: KMS rotation test must be executable using existing operator tooling/APIs without manual secret copying or keyboard-based paste of keys.
Compatibility: the upgrade must be compatible with customers running split-horizon DNS and private registries; acceptance requires a successful dry-run with private registry mirrors configured.
Time-to-detect: any class-0 failure (data corruption, persistent node split) must be detected and trigger rollback within 5 minutes of occurrence during the canary window.

Regulatory constraints: for deployments with retention or export controls, the process must not cause any telemetry to be exfiltrated beyond permitted endpoints; verification must include a telemetry-gate check.

Recovery validation: after rollback, previously warm caches and KV state either must be restored to within 95% of pre-upgrade hit-rate or an acceptable plan must be produced and executed within the maintenance window.
Test repeatability: the entire canary + partition + KMS rotation sequence must be codified in a test orchestrator script and runnable in staging by SRE without manual steps.
test_plan: Stage a dedicated canary cluster in an isolated VPC mirroring production network policies.
Deploy current release to baseline nodes and run workload to capture baseline metrics for 24 hours.
Trigger canary deployment to 5% of nodes and start synthetic workload with seeded KV prefixes to exercise cache paths.
At T+10 minutes, inject a one-way partition between canary and control plane for 90 seconds; observe behaviors and collect traces.
At T+25 minutes, inject symmetric packet loss at 10% for 3 minutes while continuing traffic.
At T+40 minutes, perform KMS rotation via automated operator API; validate key audit events and decryption success across components.
At T+70 minutes, verify p99/p50 metrics, error rates, and run post-upgrade integrity checks against stored embeddings and model artifacts.
If all checks pass, promote rollout to next tranche (e.g., 20%) and repeat; otherwise, trigger automated rollback and record incident ticket.
Run the full sequence at least three times in staging with different seed traffic profiles before approving GA release.
Include a scheduled tabletop drill with SRE and Customer Success to exercise manual rollback and postmortem procedures.
rollback_plan: Automated gate: define programmatic checks that will halt rollout and flip traffic away from canary cohort if thresholds breached.
Safe image pin: maintain last-known-good image digest and an automated revert job that can restore nodes within the rollback SLA.
State reconciliation: for KV-cache inconsistencies provide a defined sequence for cache invalidation and controlled re-warm to avoid mass cold-start spikes.

KMS reversion: if key rotation causes decryption failures, have a non-destructive fallback that re-introduces the previous key copy for decryption-only operations while preserving rotation audit trail.
Operator escalation: clearly document who to call for out-of-band emergency (SRE lead, PM on-call, Security contact) and required Slack/phone steps.
out_of_scope: Design or implementation of vendor KMS services (we assume the customer's KMS supports rotation APIs),
Large-scale fleet upgrades beyond canary tranches (this ticket defines the canary contract only),
Changes to customer application-level migration logic unrelated to runtime or serving stack.
open_questions: What is the minimum achievable canary size for very small customer clusters?
Do we require signed attestations from customer-run proxy mirrors for egress exceptions, or will operator-acknowledged permits suffice?
Should the KMS rotation test include cross-region key replication verification for multi-region Private deployments?
What telemetry retention window is required to satisfy auditability for regulated customers?
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Decided to adopt a 5% default canary tranche for initial rollouts (PM + SRE).
2026-02-25: Chose to require signed image artifacts for air-gapped deployments (Security + Infra).
2026-03-05: Agreed to implement KMS rotation path via existing operator APIs and avoid manual secret copying (PM + Security).
risks: Simulated partitions may not surface subtle state-corruption bugs that only occur under long-lived splits.
KMS vendors may have pre-existing constraints that require temporary egress; negotiating proxies could delay timelines.
Automatic rollback in some edge cases could cause cache storms that temporarily increase latency for remaining healthy nodes.
notes: Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to identify representative customer traffic profiles for the synthetic workload.
Engage the Security team early to define acceptable egress proxy endpoints and an approval workflow for customers in highly regulated environments.
Plan for a feature flag gating the simulated network injection so it can be disabled quickly in live environments.
